messages.text: my baby is 9 months and I'm still nursing. it's just us two. could we get WIC? I make $2,500 a month

Yes, WIC could be a good fit. A mom who is nursing a baby under 1 can often get it. I need two quick things to check:

1. How old are you?
2. Is the $2,500 a month your pay from a job, before taxes are taken out?
I'm 26. And yeah, the $2,500 is from my job, before taxes.

**WIC looks likely for you and your baby.** The next step is to apply at a local health department clinic, or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). The Tennessee Department of Health has more at https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html.

**Why WIC looks likely**
- WIC serves women who are breastfeeding a baby under 1, and it serves the baby too ([7 CFR 246.2, WIC definitions](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2)).
- Your income is $2,500 a month. WIC's limit for 2 people is $3,337 a month ([USDA WIC guidelines, July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926)).
- The clinic will also do a short health and nutrition check ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7)).

**Other help you might get**
- **TennCare for your baby looks likely.** Children under 1 can get it at income up to $3,517 a month for a household of 2. Your income is under that. Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html). Apply at https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/ or call 855-259-0701.
- **TennCare for you looks unlikely.** The limit for parents is $1,804 a month, and your income is over that. You can still apply.
- **Food assistance (SNAP) is possible.** The estimate is about $27 a month. That's only an estimate.
  - Your income is over the official federal limit of $2,345 ([USDA FY 2027 limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola)).
  - Tennessee's limit is unsettled. News reports say the state raised it to 200% of poverty, which would cover you ([Hoodline, June 2026](https://hoodline.com/2026/06/snap-shakeup-could-put-more-food-on-memphis-tables/)). No official source has confirmed that yet.
  - It's still worth applying. You can apply at https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application or call 866-311-4287.
  - I didn't count rent, utilities, or child care. If you pay any of those, tell me and I can run it again. They could raise the estimate.
  - Under federal rules, savings are limited to $3,000 in cash and bank accounts.

You can also dial 211 for free help finding and applying for local programs.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and you can apply for any of these programs.
